steps: The claim is causal ('prevents') and refers to memory decline over time in adults 65 and older.
The only evidence is a one-time cross-sectional survey with a single memory test per person. Daily green tea drinkers scored slightly higher.
Daily drinkers were also more physically active and more often had higher education, and the comparison was not adjusted for these differences. The association is therefore confounded.
A single test cannot show decline, and nothing identifies a causal effect. The core error is inferring causation from a confounded association.
uncertainties: The context does not say whether green tea has no effect; it only fails to support the causal claim.
The survey design, comparison type and effect size beyond 'slightly higher' are not reported in detail.
Only the supplied context was reviewed; no external search was run.
